world.name: The Standing Room
world.summary: The exactness of a record, kept in a room where people actually know each other.
world.naming_direction: Record-keeping words with a human room around them: standing, entry, bench.

sample_names.name: Standing
sample_names.rationale: What a student builds, said the way a teammate would say it.

sample_names.name: The Bench
sample_names.rationale: Who you can call on, without implying a ranking.

world.tagline_direction: Flat statements of fact rather than promises — what happened, who confirmed it.
voice_rules: State the fact, then say it the way a teammate would.
Use numbers where a number exists.
No exclamation marks; the warmth is in the words.
world.voice_sample_line: Four projects finished, three teammates confirmed it — and two of them would work with you again.

typography.rationale: Keeps the human warmth at the top of the page.
The record itself stays monospaced and exact.

imagery: Screenshots of the record itself, never stock photos of students laughing
Close crops of handwriting, stamps and signatures
composition: Left-aligned rows, generous line spacing, no centred hero text
Rules and dividers instead of cards and shadows
world.audience_perception: Serious and slightly institutional — reassuring to someone who has been let down, cold to someone looking for friends.
risks: Can feel like a credit score for people
Little warmth to attract students who have not yet been burned
opportunities: The only student brand that looks like evidence rather than marketing
Ages well: the record gets more valuable every term
obvious_ideas_rejected: A friendly campus-blue app with rounded corners — the default student-product look.
A trust-badge and five-star world — the marketplace pattern, which turns classmates into ratings.

outputs.merge_note: Kept the factual record from The Ledger as the core, and took Crew Room's voice and palette so it reads as a room rather than a database. Dropped the dark interface.
